$comment: The Upskilling Labs home page (src/pages/index.astro): one journey of nineteen scenes over a live world, the words beside the picture. The idea it shows: The Labs is one big open project. Everyone in it builds three things together (open workshops and playbooks, the method and kits that turn strangers into teams doing real work, and the platform every Lab runs on), and a small team at the centre curates the official versions every Lab gets. The Build Cycle is the engine: real work, start to finish; when cohorts hit obstacles, Mentors build the next workshops around them; what works is shared back. Everything after the account happens inside it. No levels, pins, membership or dues here.

model.$comment: The world (src/scripts/orbnet.ts), held on screen through the journey: the camera travels its eighteen scenes as you scroll, and the motif changes shape with them: the system; three of its orbits drawn down into a vortex beneath the orb and wound into one triple helix (the weave); down the helix to each path's own thread, where small scenes play out on it (workshops coming down Learn's thread; strangers becoming a Pod, then teams, a knot freed by a workshop, the Showcase on Build's; contributions rising up Share's to the centre, which sends the official version out to every Lab); the weave again; and the system again, a new Lab born. Its words: the orb's button, the pause, and what pointing at anything says.

intro.lede: Work is changing too fast to figure out alone. So we don't. The Upskilling Labs is a free community of people near you, figuring it out together, in person.
intro.terms: No tech background needed. Join once, and three paths open up.

threads.$comment: Joining is the one action; it opens three paths that weave together. "It" is the work: real projects, start to finish. In the world (src/scripts/orbnet.ts) the paths are three of the system's own orbits drawn down into one triple helix. `then` is what each path's way in says at the close.

threads.lede: It's the work: real projects, start to finish, with people you meet here. Learn what it takes, build it together, and share what works.

build.title: Make something real.
build.lede: A Build Cycle is the whole of the work, start to finish: framing a problem, forming a team, making something that lasts, and delivering it.

journey.$comment: The journey's scenes between the intro and the close, in order. Each is one idea, shown by the world and said beside it in a line or two.

open.title: One big open project.
open.lede: Everything here is made in the open by the people in it: the workshops, the way a Build Cycle runs, and the platform it all runs on. A small team at the centre curates the official versions, and every Lab gets them.
open.story: It began inside a library: a pilot at DC Public Library in fall 2025, fifty former federal workers navigating career change together. Now it's open to every professional, city by city.

workshops.title: Every workshop starts with a real obstacle.
workshops.lede: Mentors build each one around something a team ran into in a Build Cycle, write it down, and improve it every time it runs. Then it's open for any Lab to use.

topics.body: The human skills the future of work runs on: communication, storytelling, and framing problems well.

topics.body: Working with AI: understanding LLMs, prompting, vibe coding, building agents.

topics.title: In step with the cycle
topics.body: Drop in whenever. Sessions track the Build Cycle, so each one gives your Pod what it needs next.

pod.title: Strangers become a Pod.
pod.lede: Pods of nine or more form around a problem situation. Most people feel unsure while Pods form, and everyone lands in one.

teams.title: Teams form around what you propose.
teams.lede: Three to five people each, with Mentors beside you. The work is heaviest at the start and the end, steady in between.

stuck.title: Every obstacle becomes a workshop.
stuck.lede: Mentors turn what teams run up against into the next workshop, so each cycle leaves the next one better equipped.

showcase.title: Show what you built.
showcase.lede: In public, and open source: real work that lasts, credited to the people who made it.

cycle.$comment: Two states, switched by date on the page itself so it never goes stale: open until `closes`, then underway. `closes` is the kickoff date until the deadline is set. In OLOS, from the cycle's own dates.

cycle.body: Twelve weeks, a Pod of curious peers, and a problem worth solving. Places are limited. It's an open cycle: the projects are open source, free for anyone to use and build on.
